title: PAR-07/S8 DataIndex payload-region boundary control
scope: Verify DataIndex local offsets cannot reinterpret payload-region bytes as record headers
Ensure a malformed row does not silently become a modeler payload association
Preserve adjacent valid record associations in the existing generated DataStorage profile

localCodeInspection: src/drw_datastorage.cpp::readDataRecords bounds each DataIndex-referenced record header to the data segment's declared object-data region before reading header fields

tests/graph_preservation_tests.cpp::testDataStorageRecordCountAlignmentAnchors already generates four records with unsorted DataIndex rows, an explicit object-data anchor, exact payload association, and modeler linking
method.limitations: Generated malformed bytes demonstrate parser boundary behavior and retained neighboring records only. They do not establish arbitrary producer compatibility, ACIS semantic validity, or consumer acceptance.

formatBasis.authority: The DataIndex→record-header lookup is checked against the documented DataStorage layout; no peer implementation is used as the expected-value oracle.
formatBasis.expectedDisposition: A row that resolves into the object-data payload region rather than a complete record-header slot is diagnosed as structurally invalid and is not used to associate a record; independently valid rows remain inspectable.

implementation.generatedCase: In the four-record profile, mutate one DataIndex local offset so its record-header location equals the object-data start; target the 20-byte suffix payload so the prefix could resemble a plausible record-header size if the region bound were bypassed.
assertions: Require the invalid handle to be absent and exactly the other three records to retain their expected payloads.

validation.commitBlocker: Shared worktree contains extensive user-owned changes; no files were staged.

decision.nextAction: Self-unblock to the next source-backed local PAR-07/S8 invariant; keep independent semantics and native consumer evidence for their separate composed gates.
